name: Vietnamese Iced Coffee
intro: Vietnamese iced coffee, or cà phê sữa đá, is strong, dark coffee dripped slowly onto sweetened condensed milk and poured over ice. It's bold, syrupy and wonderfully sweet, with a deep roasted flavor. A little goes a long way on a hot day.
heroAlt: Engraved line illustration of Vietnamese iced coffee with condensed milk

vessel.name: Short glass filled with ice
vessel.note: Use a heatproof glass for the hot brew.

ingredients.note: Medium-coarse grind. Dark roasts, often including robusta, are traditional in Vietnam.
Adjust to taste next time, but this is the base recipe.
Just off the boil, around 195 to 205°F.

equipment.alternative: AeroPress, French press or small pour-over (see home methods)

steps.title: Add the condensed milk
steps.body: Spoon 2 tbsp of sweetened condensed milk into the bottom of a heatproof glass. The coffee will drip right onto it and start melting it.
steps.tip: Warm the glass slightly to help it blend.

steps.title: Set up the phin
steps.body: Place the phin on top of the glass, add 2 tbsp of ground coffee, and gently shake level. Press the filter insert on lightly. Too much pressure slows the drip too much.
steps.tip: Press just enough to even the surface.

steps.title: Bloom
steps.body: Pour a splash of hot water over the grounds, just enough to wet them, and wait about 30 seconds. This lets the coffee swell and degas, helping extraction be even.

steps.title: Slow drip
steps.body: Fill the phin with the remaining hot water, up to a total of 4 oz, and cover it with the lid. Let it drip slowly, about 4 to 5 minutes. The slow drip makes a strong, concentrated brew.
steps.tip: If it drips in under 2 minutes, grind finer or press a bit harder. If it barely drips, grind coarser.

steps.title: Stir
steps.body: Remove the phin and stir the coffee thoroughly with the condensed milk until blended into a caramel-colored syrup. Taste it, as it should be sweet and strong.

steps.title: Pour over ice
steps.body: Fill a second glass with ice, then pour the coffee over it, or add ice directly if the glass is big enough. Stir and serve.
steps.tip: Pour slowly over ice to avoid splashes.

homeMethods.note: Use a medium-fine grind, 2 tbsp coffee and about 4 oz of hot water, then press into the condensed milk. It's a great substitute and gives a strong, clean cup, though less syrupy than phin-drip.
Steep 2 tbsp of dark coffee with 4 oz of hot water for about 4 minutes, plunge into condensed milk. The result is bold but a bit lighter and less concentrated than phin coffee.

homeMethods.method: Moka pot or strong brewed coffee
homeMethods.note: A small moka pot brew or double-strength drip coffee poured over condensed milk will give a similar sweet, strong drink. It misses some of the phin's slow-drip intensity.

tips: Dark, bold coffee stands up best to the sweet milk.
Condensed milk is very sweet, so taste and adjust the amount in future batches.
Brands and roast styles in Vietnam vary, and some include chicory or other additions.
commonMistakes: Grinding too fine and getting a drip that stalls.
Skipping the bloom and getting uneven extraction.
Not stirring the condensed milk in fully.
Using a light roast that tastes thin and sour next to the sweetness.

variations.name: Hot cà phê sữa
variations.description: Skip the ice and serve it hot, with the coffee dripped onto condensed milk in a small cup.

variations.name: Coconut coffee
variations.description: Use coconut condensed milk or coconut cream for a tropical twist.

variations.name: Egg coffee (cà phê trứng)
variations.description: A Vietnamese specialty topped with whipped egg yolk and sweetened milk. It's a separate, more involved drink.

history: Condensed milk is often said to have become common in Vietnamese coffee because fresh milk was hard to get and store, a story widely told but not fully documented. Coffee growing in Vietnam began in the French colonial era in the 1800s.

seo.title: How to Make Vietnamese Iced Coffee (Cà Phê Sữa Đá)
seo.description: Make bold, sweet Vietnamese iced coffee with dark coffee, sweetened condensed milk and ice. Includes phin and no-phin methods.
